  "markdown_report": "**Proposed direction: candidate-competition auditing for the existing HSTU.** At 0% progress, prioritize a diagnostic that tests whether strong training-pair separation survives more plausible competition before changing training.

**Starting insights.** (1) Mean training margins are 9.64–10.94 across categories, with negative-win rates below 0.2%. These measurements establish separation from supplied negatives, while validation ranking remains unmeasured. (2) Final-event deletion reduces margins by 3.10–4.06, whereas prefix shuffling changes means by at most 0.01. This motivates examining recent-item associations, although deletion changes readout and cannot establish a shortcut. (3) Qualitative feedback distinguishes broad relatedness from usefulness. Titles and descriptions can identify plausible competitors, but cannot establish ownership, fulfilled needs, or compatibility when specifications are missing.

**Related-work insights.** (1) Sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons [1]. Alternative candidate panels should therefore be labeled stress tests, with host HR@10 unchanged. (2) Hard-negative mining encounters false negatives [2]. Similar unobserved items must remain unlabeled competitors rather than confirmed mistakes. (3) Product-recommendation taxonomies distinguish compatibility from insufficient evidence [3]. Missing textual specifications should produce unknown judgments, never inferred incompatibility.

**Framework and directions.** Organize investigation by competition difficulty, historical dependence, and evidence sufficiency:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Next measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Competition | Easy training-pair separation | Fixed candidate-panel ranks |
| History | Endpoint-dominated sensitivity | Candidate-specific prefix sensitivity |
| Evidence | Broad relevance, uncertain usefulness | Specification evidence coverage |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fixed competition panels** [1,2] | 4/7/3 | Originality: useful HSTU integration; potential: exposes competition gaps; difficulty: reuses scoring hooks | Originality: established sampling; potential: no proven uplift; difficulty: candidate eligibility needs care |
| Prefix-only item dropout during training | 3/5/4 | Originality: targeted ablation; potential: tests history robustness; difficulty: preserves backbone | Originality: standard augmentation; potential: may erase useful context; difficulty: requires retraining and validation |
| Evidence-backed specification audit [3] | 5/6/6 | Originality: connects evidence to ranking; potential: distinguishes unknowns; difficulty: no pretrained weights needed | Originality: established taxonomy; potential: sparse text limits coverage; difficulty: normalization requires auditing |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze sampled training histories and their original final-position positives. Score three equally sized, deterministic panels: uniform catalog competitors, competitors matched to the positive’s training-frequency bin, and title/description TF–IDF neighbors. Exclude padding, the positive, and observed row-history items; without verified user identities, call these *row-unobserved*, not user-unseen.

Report positive rank, panel-relative margin, and competitor overlap, with eligibility counts and frequency strata. These are training-history stress measurements, not validation HR@10 or estimates of full-catalog accuracy. Preserve identity controls, final-nonpadding readout, diagnostic interfaces, all four routes, and one unchanged HSTU checkpoint per category. No training or predictor modification is required; subsequent training hypotheses remain subject to pinned macro validation HR@10.",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Add a deterministic candidate-competition audit to the family-specific HSTU diagnostic adapter. For each eligible sampled training history, retain its original final-position positive and compare its rank against equal-sized uniform, training-frequency-matched, and lexical-neighbor competitor panels. Keep the existing model, checkpoint, predictor, and host evaluation unchanged.",
    "motivation": "Supplied diagnostics show very strong separation from sampled training negatives, while qualitative feedback identifies broadly related recommendations with uncertain immediate usefulness. Candidate-panel contrasts can reveal whether separation depends on easy competitors without claiming that plausible alternatives are irrelevant or that stress-test results predict validation gains.",
    "implementation_notes": "Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and every ModelView interface. Use view.model.eval() and torch.no_grad(), restoring the original mode in finally. Cache at most ten batches and use local seed-42 generators without changing training RNG state. Derive catalog eligibility from the host real-item mapping; never assume every embedding row represents a real item. Build frequency counts exclusively from user_train['History']. Build a bounded sparse TF–IDF index exclusively from available titles/descriptions, with no downloads or pretrained weights. Missing text makes a row ineligible for the lexical contrast and must be counted. Read final positions using masked physical indices, never sequence length minus one. Retain original positive and negative targets for existing diagnostics. For new panels, exclude padding, reserved tokens, the positive, and every observed item in that row. Loader identities are None, so do not claim complete user-history exclusion or user-level uncertainty. Freeze panels of 99 unique competitors where all three pools support that size; otherwise report ineligibility rather than silently reducing or filling a panel. Specify frequency-bin boundaries before scoring. For lexical panels, select the highest TF–IDF cosine competitors deterministically, breaking ties by item ID; require nonzero textual similarity and report resulting coverage. Compare panels on their common eligible rows and separately report all panel-specific counts. Score through predict_score using feature shape B x 1 x D and item shape B x 1 x 100, or bounded chunks respecting the existing adapter. Define conservative positive rank as 1 plus the number of competitor scores greater than or equal to its score. Report rank quantiles, tie counts, positive-minus-maximum-competitor margin, and pairwise panel overlap. Label any top-10 inclusion statistic as a training-history panel statistic, never host HR@10. Keep supplied geometry, identity, and paired perturbation diagnostics with their definitions. Null values require explicit reasons. No ownership, satisfaction, compatibility, simulator-trait, or causal-preference conclusions follow from these measurements. The interpretation prompt must embed measured values, definitions, coverage, and limitations. Any later training experiment retains DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, all four categories, and exactly one independently trained HSTU checkpoint per category; checkpoint averaging and separately fitted score fusion remain prohibited.",
    "pseudocode": "class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Integrate with, and retain, the supplied diagnostic implementation.
        real_items = host_real_item_ids(self.view)
        frequencies = counts_from_public_training_histories(self.view.user_train)
        lexical_index = sparse_tfidf_from_titles_and_descriptions(self.view.meta_data)
        rng = local_generator(seed=42)
        was_training = self.view.model.training
        self.view.model.eval()
        try:
            with torch.no_grad():
                for batch_id, (_, seq, pos, neg) in first_ten_batches(train_loader):
                    physical = torch.arange(seq.shape[1], device=seq.device)
                    end = physical[None, :].expand_as(seq).masked_fill(seq.eq(0), -1).amax(1)
                    eligible = end.ge(0)
                    # Gather only eligible rows; do not index an empty row at -1.
                    rows = eligible.nonzero().flatten()
                    target = pos[rows, end[rows]]
                    rows, target = retain_real_nonzero_targets(rows, target, real_items)
                    features = self.view.log2feats(seq)
                    final = features[rows, end[rows]].unsqueeze(1)
                    assert_identity_scores_match(self.view, seq, rows, end, target)
                    for local_row, row in enumerate(rows):
                        excluded = nonzero_ids(seq[row]) | {int(target[local_row])}
                        pools = build_uniform_frequency_and_lexical_pools(
                            real_items, excluded, target[local_row], frequencies,
                            lexical_index, fixed_frequency_bins=True)
                        panels, missingness = freeze_unique_panels(
                            pools, size=99, rng=rng, lexical_tie_break='item_id')
                        record_eligibility(batch_id, row, missingness)
                        if all_panels_available(panels):
                            for name, competitors in panels.items():
                                candidates = prepend(target[local_row], competitors)
                                scores = self.view.predict_score(
                                    final[local_row:local_row+1],
                                    candidates.reshape(1, 1, 100))
                                record_finite_rank_margin_ties_and_overlap(
                                    scores, panels, batch_id, row, name)
                metrics = summarize_descriptively_on_common_eligible_rows()
                return {'metrics': merge_with_retained_baseline_metrics(metrics),
                        'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions_and_missingness()}
        finally:
            self.view.model.train(was_training)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(
        measurements=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        instructions='Distinguish training-panel stress measurements from host validation; '
                     'retain unknown judgments and coverage; propose hypotheses without '
                     'causal preference claims or numerical uplift forecasts.')",
    "originality": {
      "score": 4,
      "positive": "Combines controlled candidate composition, lexical evidence, and explicit missingness within the existing HSTU diagnostic contract.",
      "negative": "Candidate sampling and hard-competitor stress testing are established methods; novelty lies mainly in careful integration."
    },
    "future_potential": {
      "score": 7,
      "positive": "Can identify competition-specific weaknesses and motivate targeted single-model training ablations while preserving benchmark comparability.",
      "negative": "Training-history stress measurements may reflect memorization and have no demonstrated relationship to held-out improvement."
    },
    "code_difficulty": {
      "score": 3,
      "positive": "Requires no retraining or architecture changes and reuses existing sequence-feature and candidate-scoring interfaces.",
      "negative": "Real-item mapping, sparse lexical retrieval, candidate eligibility, and descriptive aggregation require careful implementation."
    }
  },
  "related_work": [
    {
      "title": "On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation",
      "link": "https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/",
      "contributions": [
        "Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield inconsistent model comparisons.",
        "Motivates treating candidate composition as part of the measurement definition."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Does not establish that the proposed stress panels predict improvements under the pinned benchmark.",
        "Does not justify replacing the host evaluator."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "SIGIR 2026 work on false negatives in hard-negative mining, supplied search result",

      "contributions": [
        "The supplied search summary identifies false negatives as a concern in hard-negative mining."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The supplied excerpt does not provide a verified paper title or quantitative findings.",
        "Supports caution about competitor labels, not a claim that lexical competitors are true negatives."
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "TREC Product Recommendations: Task and Annotation Definitions",
      "link": "https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html",
      "contributions": [
        "Distinguishes substitutes, complements, compatibility judgments, and insufficient evidence.",
        "Provides a useful vocabulary for interpreting qualitative recommendation failures."
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Product relationships do not establish current user demand, ownership, or satisfaction.",
        "Applying the taxonomy requires evidence unavailable for some items in this task."
      ]
    }
  ]
